subject: chemistry

moments.title: Avogadro's hypothesis
moments.body:
Avogadro proposes that equal volumes of gases at the same T and P contain the same number of particles — and that elemental gases such as O2 are diatomic, not monatomic. The idea resolves Dalton's contradictions about water (HO vs H2O).

The paper is ignored for 50 years.
moments.takeaway: The right answer about molecules and atoms, ignored for half a century.

moments.title: Karlsruhe Congress
moments.body: At the first international chemistry conference, Cannizzaro circulates a pamphlet defending Avogadro's hypothesis. The argument persuades Mendeleev and Meyer; the periodic table follows within a decade.
moments.takeaway: The first international scientific congress saves a 49-year-old neglected idea.

moments.title: Perrin measures Avogadro's number
moments.body: Using Brownian motion, Perrin measures Avogadro's number to within 10% of the modern value. The energeticist resistance collapses; atoms are now experimental fact.
moments.takeaway: Avogadro's number measured directly — and the atomic theory is settled.

moments.title: Mole redefined
moments.body: The mole is redefined as exactly 6.02214076 × 10^23 entities — Avogadro's number is now an exact constant by definition, not measurement.
moments.takeaway: Avogadro's number becomes an exact mathematical constant of the SI.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: The mole is one of seven SI base units. Modern stoichiometry, gas laws and titration calculations all rest on Avogadro's hypothesis.
now.open_questions: What are the smallest physical samples we can synthesise — single-molecule chemistry?

reflection: Avogadro got the right answer in 1811 and was ignored. The Karlsruhe Congress finally heard him. What does it take to overcome 50 years of neglect?
